discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller and co-workers showed theoretically (1998) that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters. Greiner and Bloch then observed the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator (2002), the first clean experimental realization of a strongly correlated lattice model with atoms. That result created the field of analog quantum simulation. Bloch and Greiner later built quantum gas microscopes that image and control single atoms at single lattice sites, revealing antiferromagnetic order, string patterns, entanglement entropy and many-body localization directly. Together these advances turned Feynman's quantum simulator idea into a working laboratory tool. They now answer questions about quantum magnetism, topology and non-equilibrium dynamics that are intractable in solids and on classical computers. The same platform led directly to today's neutral-atom quantum processors. This discovery transformed atomic physics and condensed-matter physics alike.
